body.statement:
Suppose \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\).  Under either \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) or \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation predictable variation satisfies, jointly over the prior and design,
\[
 G_nQ_n\xrightarrow{L^2}
 \begin{cases}
 [Mp(1-p)]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
 [Mp(1-p)]^{-1}-2\rho/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), under either prior,
\[
 \mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\!\left\{
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}\!\left(
 \left|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|>\varepsilon\mid Y\right)>\varepsilon
 \right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
We compute the predictable variation for the stipulated filtration.  Put \(q_n=1-p_n\), \(d_i=x_{i1}-x_{i0}\), and, for realized block \(A_g\),
\[
 c_g=\frac{h_{1,n}(A_g)}{p_n}+\frac{h_{0,n}(A_g)}{q_n}.
\]
Averaging first over the treatment labels shows that the martingale at unit-reveal time \(N_n\) equals the simple-random-sample mean \(N_n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}d_{U_j}\), centered at \(n^{-1}\sum_id_i\).  The remaining label-randomization residual is
\[
 \frac1{G_n}\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}(Z_g-p_n)c_g. \qquad\text{(2)}
\]
Thus \(Q_n=Q_n^U+Q_n^L\), the sums of conditional variances over the two consecutive reveal phases.

Let \(\mu_{r-1}^d\) and \(v_{r-1}^d\) be the mean and the denominator-population variance of the \(n-r+1\) unit values remaining just before unit reveal \(r\).  If \(N_n<n\), direct subtraction of the two successive conditional sample means gives
\[
 D_{n,r}^U=\frac{n-N_n}{N_n(n-r)}(d_{U_r}-\mu_{r-1}^d),\qquad
 Q_n^U=\sum_{r=1}^{N_n}\frac{(n-N_n)^2}{N_n^2(n-r)^2}v_{r-1}^d. \qquad\text{(3)}
\]
If \(N_n=n\), this phase is identically zero.  Under the common prior \(d_i=0\).  Under the independent prior the permuted \(d_i\) are iid, bounded, mean zero, and variance two.  If \(\rho<1\), all remaining populations in (3) have order \(n\), and the elementary bound \(\mathbb E|v_{r-1}^d-2|\le C(n-r+1)^{-1/2}\), obtained by expanding the empirical first two moments, applies.  Moreover, with \(L_n=n-N_n\),
\[
 G_n\sum_{r=1}^{N_n}\frac{L_n^2}{N_n^2(n-r)^2}
 =\frac{L_n^2}{MN_n}\sum_{j=L_n}^{n-1}j^{-2}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{M}. \qquad\text{(4)}
\]
If \(\rho=1\) and \(L_n\ge1\), the left side of (4) is at most \((1+L_n)/(MN_n)\to0\); it is zero when \(L_n=0\).  Equations (3)--(4) therefore give
\[
 G_nQ_n^U\xrightarrow{L^1}
 \begin{cases}0,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\2(1-\rho)/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.\end{cases} \qquad\text{(5)}
\]

For the label phase, let \(s\) labels have been exposed, let
\[
 \pi_{s-1}=\frac{G_{1n}-\sum_{j<s}Z_j}{G_n-s+1},\qquad
 \bar c_{s+1:G_n}=\frac1{G_n-s}\sum_{j>s}c_j.
\]
Subtracting successive conditional expectations in (2) gives, for \(s<G_n\),
\[
 D_{n,N_n+s}^L=\frac{Z_s-\pi_{s-1}}{G_n}
 (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G_n}),
\]
and the final increment is zero.  Hence
\[
 G_nQ_n^L=\frac1{G_n}\sum_{s=1}^{G_n-1}
 \pi_{s-1}(1-\pi_{s-1})(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G_n})^2. \qquad\text{(6)}
\]
The label process is independent of the \(c_g\)'s.  If \(L=G_n-s+1\), direct hypergeometric covariance algebra gives
\[
 \mathbb E(\pi_{s-1}-p_n)^2
 =p_nq_n\frac{G_n-L}{L(G_n-1)}.
\]
Since \(|x(1-x)-p_nq_n|\le2|x-p_n|\), averaging the square roots of these variances over \(L=2,\ldots,G_n\) shows that replacing every weight in (6) by \(p_nq_n\) changes (6) by \(o_{L^1}(1)\); boundedness of \(c_g\) is uniform because \(p_n,q_n\) are eventually bounded away from zero.

Under either prior the disjoint blocks contain independent prior signs, so \(c_1,\ldots,c_{G_n}\) are iid, bounded, and centered.  The reverse updating identity
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{G_n-1}\frac{G_n-s}{G_n-s+1}
 (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G_n})^2
 =\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}(c_g-\bar c)^2. \qquad\text{(7)}
\]
is obtained by expanding both sides recursively.  The difference between the unweighted sum on the left of (7) and its weighted version is \(O(\log G_n)\), because \(c_g\) is uniformly bounded.  The iid law of large numbers applied to the right side therefore shows that the unweighted average in (6) converges in \(L^1\) to \(\operatorname{Var}(c_1)\).  Now
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(c_1)=
 \begin{cases}
 [Mp_n^2q_n^2]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
 M^{-1}(p_n^{-2}+q_n^{-2}),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
 \end{cases}
\]
It follows from (6) that
\[
 G_nQ_n^L\xrightarrow{L^1}
 \begin{cases}
 [Mpq]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
 M^{-1}(q/p+p/q),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
 \end{cases} \qquad\text{(8)}
\]
Adding (5) and (8), and using \(q/p+p/q+2=1/(pq)\), proves the two asserted constants.  Indeed, the coefficient sum in (4) is at most \(1/M\), because it contains \(N_n\) terms and each is at most \(L_n^{-2}\), and (6) is bounded by the uniform envelope for \(c_g^2\).  Thus all scaled quantities in (3) and (6) are uniformly bounded; the \(L^1\) convergence upgrades to \(L^2\).  In particular, \(\operatorname{Var}(G_nQ_n)=o(1)\), which is the requested normalized-variance check.

Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} gives convergence in prior probability of \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) to the same strictly positive constants.  Thus \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\to1\) jointly in prior and design probability.  If
\[
 b_n(Y)=\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
 \left(|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>\varepsilon\mid Y\right),
\]
then joint convergence says \(\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n}b_n(Y)\to0\).  Markov's inequality gives \(\mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\{b_n(Y)>\varepsilon\}\to0\), proving the final assertion.
